text:
arjun: quick follow-up on the dedicated pool orchestration split — after the RFC, we still need to decide which component owns 'elastic headroom' and burst lane admission. want to lock this before the larger refactor so we don't end up with two sources of truth.

katie: +1. my current tilt: operator owns durable headroom/reservoir accounting and admission policy, runtime owns per-request inflight accounting and immediate fallbacks. keeps state local and durable decisions centralized.

noah: agree with katie. operationally we should expose a very small admission RPC so runtime can query for short leases instead of owning long-term state. keeps operator testable and auditable.

jess: can we sketch a minimal proto for that RPC? will help with tests and the console integration.

arjun: quick sketch below (very small):
```
service PoolAdmission {
  rpc RequestAdmission(AdmissionRequest) returns (AdmissionReply) {}
}
message AdmissionRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  int32 slots = 2;
  int32 max_latency_ms = 3;
  bool burst = 4; // short-lived burst intent
  string sla_tier = 5; // optional: enterprise/free
}
message AdmissionReply {
  bool granted = 1;
  int32 lease_ms = 2;
  string reason = 3; // e.g. "headroom", "preemptible", "overflow"
  string fallback_model = 4; // optional: model id to use if denied
}
```

katie: nice. also need a read-only Intents / Snapshot API so console and autoscaler can reconcile what operator thinks the headroom is without constantly mutating.

noah: two operational concerns: 1) cardinality if we track per-tenant burst tokens; 2) how to reconcile clock drift when lease_ms expires. suggestion: aggregate tokens into sliding buckets (1m/1h) to reduce cardinality and have runtime best-effort clock sync with small safety margin.

arjun: sounds good. operator persists compacted reservoir windows in etcd; runtime keeps ephemeral inflight counters locally and only calls RequestAdmission on cache-miss or when wants a lease for a burst.

jess: test plan idea: synthetic tenants with gradual baseline + bursty spikes, verify admission grants, fallback behavior, and metrics emitted. also assert that operator decisions survive operator restart (durability).

noah: for metrics, emit per-tenant aggregated counters only on heavy events to avoid high cardinality. we can also expose a sample-rate for telemetry.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline started for branch control-surface-refactor by @arjun — build 1/3 succeeded.

katie: one more policy thing: add an SLA prioritization flag in AdmissionRequest so operator can fast-path enterprise tenants and apply different reservoir rules.

arjun: agreed. updated proto above includes sla_tier. decision summary so far:
- operator: owns reservoir accounting, long-term quotas, durable admission policies, and the Intents/Snapshot read surface
- runtime: owns per-request inflight accounting, short-lived leases, local caches, and immediate fallback logic when denied
- admission surface: tiny RPC (RequestAdmission) returning short leases + fallback hints
- telemetry surface: read-only snapshot for console/autoscaler reconciliation, sampled metrics to avoid cardinality explosion

action items:
- @noah prototype compacted reservoir store layout + eviction compaction (due Wed)
- @jess implement chaos tests for admission denial and operator restart durability (due Fri)
- @katie add SLA flag to proto + ops e2e (due Mon)
- @arjun open PR with proto, README, and short design note (due Tue)

noah: SGTM, i'll draft the store layout and share a short example of compaction windows.

jess: starting the test harness this afternoon, will try to simulate 200 tenants with mixed traffic.

arjun: thanks — if nobody objects i'll make the PR this week and tag people for review. happy to revisit any edgecases in the runtime sync. :thumbsup:
